newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Moscovici repeats commitment to on-time EMU.
newsitem.headline: French Moscovici repeats commitment to on-time EMU.

text.p: A delay to European economic and monetary union (EMU) would be dangerous, and France's new government remains committed to ensuring France will be ready to join a single currency in 1999, French European Affairs minister Pierre Moscovici said on Wednesday.

"The French position has been very consistent. It's that monetary union must be launched according to the terms of the Maastricht Treaty and on the scheduled date," he told reporters after a cabinet meeting.

"My personal position has always been that a delay would be a very bad thing because it would open a whole Pandora's box," he said. He said it would spark a whole series of "temptations" but did not elaborate.
He repeated that the new Socialist-led government's policy was to prepare France to join a single European currency in 1999.
